texts.preamble: Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 6 May, 2022
texts.facts: The fact that more than 57 other persons were also so infected - but fortunately, without any fatal complications - also spurred us into this motion. A particular food item is ascribed to be the probable cause. We are, like every other citizen, appalled- not only of the terribly unfortunate turn of events, but pondering how it could happen at all when strict enforcement and analytical regimes and systems are already in place under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for brevity). We are fully cognizant, as we are also told by Sri.S.Kannan, Senior Government Pleader, that necessary investigations are going on; and therefore, that it is now too early to draw conclusions. But we are firm that this shall never recur, especially because the food preparation in question appears to have obtained great popularity in our State. Therefore, though we propose not to speak specifically about the incident in focus; or to, in any manner, reflect on the ongoing investigation into it, we deem it pressing in the interests of the health and life of our citizens, to seek explication from the Authorities concerned on the measures taken, or to be taken, to warrant to them in future the safety of the food they are served and offered. This is all the more acme, since the Commissionerate of of Food Safety in Kerala is invested with the duty to implement and ensure the efficient implementation of food safety, its standards and other unexpendable requirements under the Act, as also under the Rules and Regulations under it. Apodictically, it is solely when the twin legal duties of enforcement and analytics with special emphasis on "watch, guard and accountability"- is discharged by the officers WP(C)No.15360 OF 2022 diligently, can the well publicized motto of the Commissionerate of Food Safety - "Safe food for Healthy Life", obtain real meaning.. For the afore, we order the Registry to register and number this case as a suo motu Public Interest Litigation, arraying the Government of Kerala, represented by the Secretary, Health & Family Welfare Department, Thiruvananthapuram and the Commissioner of Food Safety, Thycaud P.O., Thiruvananthapuram, as the initial respondents.
texts.arguments: 3. Today, Sri.S.Kannan - learned Senior Government Pleader, has placed on record - along with the reports of the Inspector of Police, Chandera, Kasaragod and that the the District Medical Officer - an interim report by the Commissioner of Food Safety, who has been arrayed as the 2nd respondent. The learned Senior Government Pleader conceded that the institution which is suspected of having caused the food poisoning did not have a valid food safety licence and that they had been, in fact, Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 6 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21050604/ 2 directed not to continue with their operations. WP(C)No.15360 OF 2022 He then added that the Commissionerate of Food Safety is very serious about ensuring the highest standards of food served to our citizens and that more than 32 squads have been set up all over the State to conduct surprise inspections, raids and such other. 4. Sri.S.Kannan then pointed out that, in the last two financial years, 12,683 samples were taken, 538 prosecutions launched, along with 832 adjudication cases. He submitted that this would clearly demonstrate the effort taken by the Commissionerate to make sure that the citizens are not faced with the situation as has been now reported, explaining that the horrific incident is unfortunate and isolated. 5. Sri.S.Kannan thereafter submitted that the Directorate of Food Safety has issued licences to various eateries and other outlets, following the imperative requirements under the Food Safety Act,2013 and that a total of 58,948 WP(C)No.15360 OF 2022 licences and 2,25,317 registrations have been issued. He added that in the last two years, more than 3,146 cases were compounded entailing a total penalty of 1,08,77,250 and impressed upon us that the officers concerned have been doing their duties diligently. 6. As regards the follow up action consequent to the horrific incident, Sri.S.Kannan submitted that additional Special Food Safety Squads have now been constituted by the Commissioner of Food Safety and that its efficiency bears testament to the fact that, in the last four days, 500 inspections have been conducted leading to 43 food business establishments being closed down. He further showed us that paragraph 11 of the report of the Commissioner of Food Safety avers that 47 notices have been issued for compounding and 115 kgs of stale meat had been destroyed, with 40 other samples being collected for lab WP(C)No.15360 OF 2022 analysis. He closed his submissions assuring this Court that inspection and enforcement activities are being done by the Commissionerate and will be continued to be done on a regular basis; and that it is only on account of such strenuous efforts taken by the department that our State won the 2nd position in National level for State Food safety index, as part of the World Food Safety Day, namely June 7, 2021.
